key_insight: Evaluator-guided LLM circuit search reduced both Toffoli and qubit counts on seven of eight tasks and discovered a new reversible architecture for prime-field modular inversion.
engineering_relevance: More resource-efficient reversible primitives could lower the cost of quantum algorithms across numerical computation, chemistry, optimization, simulation, and number theory.
method: Use LLMs to propose circuit designs within an evolutionary search.
Independently verify and score candidates to guide optimization.
Explore reversible architectures, including one that makes divsteps viable for modular inversion.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports significant Toffoli and qubit reductions versus the state of the art on seven tasks, plus an improved Toffoli–qubit trade-off for modular inversion on the eighth.
watch_item: The abstract does not report hardware demonstrations or search costs, leaving practical execution benefits and optimization overhead unclear.
paper_title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
